To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of a per-VC buffer management policy and the use of selective acknowledgments are both effective in improving the throughput and fairness of TCP over UBT.

1) early cell discard and selective acknowledgements are effective in improving the performance of TCP connections over ATM-UBR, and 2) per-VC accounting based buffer management policies provide significant improvement in TCP performance over the UBR service.

the performance of TCP connections over UBR can be improved by: 1) employing a per VC buffer management policy that drops the first packet in a window when congestion is encountered, and 2) employing a TCP sender that uses a congestion avoidance algorithm with selective acknowledgments.
In summary, our research is concerned with
improving the performance of TCP connections running over ATM UBR with limited buffer space in the network.
improving TCP performance over ATM UBR.
the design of a buffer management policy for ATM switches and a congestion control policy for TCP end systems that can be deployed in a network with limited buffers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of selective acknowledgment is essential to achieve high throughput and good fairness.
TCP can be made to work reasonably well over UBR with the use of appropriate switch and end system policies.
a combination of intelligent drop policy and selective acknowledgments at the end system provides the best performance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the performance of TCP can be significantly improved over ATM UBR service by using a per VC accounting based buffer management policy in the network, and a selective acknowledgement based congestion avoidance policy at the end system.
the use of a combination of early packet discard and a per-VC buffer management policy can improve TCP throughput and fairness.

with limited buffers in the ATM network, the best performance is achieved by a combination of early packet discard and per VC buffer management with selective acknowledgment and fast retransmit/recovery.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a combination of end system policies such as selective acknowledgement and fast retransmit, and network policies such as per VC accounting based early drop, can provide a good tradeoff between performance and fairness.
a combination of end system and switch policies can significantly improve the performance of a UBR network with limited buffering.

with intelligent switch drop policies, TCP performance over UBT can be improved to the level of TCP over a lossless network, and with intelligent end system congestion control, TCP performance over a lossy network can be improved.
